svg.aria-label: As-built CN2 interception: Momcozy controller and front panel wired through all four channels of a BSS138 level converter to a XIAO ESP32-C3.
svg.text: CN2 interception — AS BUILT, straight-through, and grouped by device

Converter channel N carries pin DN, and the HV side groups by device: ch1/ch2 are the controller, ch3/ch4 the panel. Every signal crosses a BSS138 channel. Only CN2 pins 1 and 2 are cut — pins 3 and 4 stay connected controller↔panel, because the panel is powered through them.
Blue = toward the ESP32 (an OEM output drives it). Green = out of the ESP32 (it drives an OEM input). Every wire keeps exactly one driver.
own MCU · owns the whole UI

g.text: The real module, in this orientation
Rotated so HV faces the machine, its pads read
HV4 · HV3 · GND · HV · HV2 · HV1 down the board,
not 1 to 4.
Wire to the printed names, not the positions.
The channel table above still applies — ch1 is HV1,
wherever HV1 happens to sit on the board.

svg.text: THE FOUR PATHS — ch1/ch2 CONTROLLER, ch3/ch4 PANEL, chN → DN
VERIFIED — ch1/ch4 unchanged; ch2/ch3 swap channels, same end-to-end

g.text: ch1 CONTROLLER pin 1 TX out → HV1 · LV1 → D1 / GPIO3 Serial0 RX
ch2 CONTROLLER pin 2 RX in ← HV2 · LV2 ← D2 / GPIO4 Serial0 TX
ch3 PANEL pin 1 RX in ← HV3 · LV3 ← D3 / GPIO5 Serial1 TX
ch4 PANEL pin 2 TX out → HV4 · LV4 → D4 / GPIO6 Serial1 RX

⚠ new channel · re-verify after rewiring
⚠ new channel, blind · re-verify
✓ 924 frames, 0 bad checksums

svg.text: The two receive paths prove themselves — every frame carries an XOR. The two transmit paths are blind, and are proven only by the far end’s watchdog staying quiet: the controller reports E5 in status byte 3 bit 6, the panel only on its display.
The pin map is not hard-coded. POST /api/detect counts edges to find the two driven pins, then reads one frame off each — header 0xA2 is the controller, 0xAA is the panel. It never drives a line.

g.text: PROTECTION — add these (none are fitted yet)
Review of the as-built module: no bulk capacitance, no transient clamp, no series damping, nothing across the relay load. Four retrofits, in the order they matter.
1 · POWER — CN2 pin 4 rail
CN2 pin4
FB1 bead 600R@100MHz
XIAO 5V
C2 100nF
C1 rides the ESP32 through supply sag when a heavy
load starts during a WiFi burst (300 mA peaks on a
rail sized for a button panel). Fit C1 AT the XIAO.
D1 SMBJ5.0A TVS across 5V/GND where the cable
enters the module — clamps switch-off transients
from the machine's relays and motors.
Brownout signature: boot_count climbs, reset_reason 15.
2 · RELAY DRIVE — GPIO10 / D10
R1 220R series
relay IN
R2 10k
pull-down (already specified)
Use an OPTO-ISOLATED module and remove the
JD-VCC jumper: coil current then comes from its
own supply, and coil kickback never reaches the
ESP32 rail. R1 damps ringing on the control line.
R2 holds the pump OFF from reset until cn2::begin().
3 · SWITCHED LOAD — 24 V pump / any coil
PUMP
cathode to +24V
Flyback diode ACROSS the load, at the load. The
relay contact interrupting an inductive 24 V pump
is the biggest transient source we are adding.
Same rule for any future solenoid valve.
AC loads (drain pump): RC snubber 100R + 100nF X2
across the contact instead — a diode cannot work on AC.
4 · LAYOUT — costs nothing, matters most
• Route the relay/pump wiring AWAY from the
four CN2 signal wires. Never in the same bundle.
• Twist 5V+GND as a pair from CN2 to the module.
• One star ground point at the shifter GND pad —
no ground loops through the relay module.
• Keep UART leads short; the 10k pull-ups on the
shifter are the line's only drive when idle.
• External antenna stays clear of the mains loom.
Evidence note: ~220k frames across 7.7 h of cycles,
0 bad checksums — the OEM loads have not corrupted
the link yet. These parts are prevention, sized for
the relay mod and supply sag, not a cure for a
problem already observed.
Fit at the next opening: C1/C2/FB1/D1 on the module, R1 in the D10 lead, D2 at the pump. Verify afterwards: POST /api/qclear, run a full cycle, bad_c/bad_p must stay 0 and boot_count must not move.
